summary: Direct authoring continued ("do everything"). v3 adds the 7 core-concept pages to the in-tree C#-developer doc tree: goal, data, channel, event, actor, call, error. Each was drafted by a Haiku subagent pointed at its spine source + the shared style brief + the v1/v2 pages, then verified: the Haiku writers corrected the briefs against source (event's real 11-event list; error's real subclass keys/statuses; Data.Merge does not exist), and I quality-read the two locked-core pages (data, call) in full and reconciled all cross-links. The tree now covers app, module(+file), type(+item), goal, data, channel, event, actor, call, error.

changes.description: Goals + steps: a goal is a loaded .pr that Start()s; app.goal = current<Goal, list>; a step dispatches to an action (cross-links the module page's .pr dispatch, not re-derived); child goals and Setup.

Data the universal carrier: the {name,type,value,properties,signature} shape (not an envelope), Data<T> + the object double-wrap footgun, the result API (Ok/FromError/Fail/Success/Error, observation-is-the-guard), navigation + lazy %var%, Properties + view tags, and the courier-vs-leaf rule.

Channels: named directional I/O owned by an actor; the Output/Error/Input role names + boot invariant (Verify); the write/read/ask surface; the channel types (stream/goal/session/message/file/noop/test); the no-Console.* rule.

The event system: the event door (item.on), the real 11 core events (start/load/create/set/remove/write/read/ask/error/hit/miss) with Before/After, bindings and clauses (a clause's handler is the module action; IClause is the binder), and module-owned events.

Actors + the execution context: System/User identities; the context as how C# reaches per-run state (App, call, Variable, Setting, FileSystem, Ok/Error/NotFound); actors own channels/settings/permissions; permissions gate the disk; how a handler gets its context.

The call stack + variable memory: a frame (goal/step/action, binding, isolated) and the keeper rule; the stack (Current/Root, Push/Isolate, overflow); frame-scoped format/settings/event; context.Variable (Get/Set/Peek, root-names-only); the variable parser for paths.

Errors: Error {message, key, status} on a Data; the subclasses with verified keys/statuses; the answer-vs-throw rule (AppException carries the Error whole, Error.FromException is the one door, carried comes back whole else ServiceError 500); error.current vs error.list.
